title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space sector is seeing a blend of strategic investments and partnerships as nations and companies seek to bolster their capabilities. Notably, the UK and Florida are pooling resources, while various firms are jockeying for position in the evolving defense landscape.

themes.title: Funding Flows and Collaborations
themes.body: The UK and Florida's joint commitment of $400,000 highlights a growing trend of regional partnerships in space. Meanwhile, German supplier deltaVision's €10.2 million raise signals that venture capital remains keen on space-related technologies.

themes.title: Defense Tech Developments
themes.body: KBR's reorganization to pursue Golden Dome work reflects a strategic pivot towards defense technology amidst rising geopolitical tensions. Simultaneously, Anduril and L3Harris's collaboration on a tactical SDA constellation bid underscores the increasing importance of integrated defense systems.

themes.title: Budget Increases for Space Resilience
themes.body: The recent FY27 budget markup adding $1.4 billion to space resilience indicates a robust commitment to enhancing national security through space. This aligns with broader trends of military focus on satellite capabilities amid rising threats.

themes.title: IPO Buzz and Market Dynamics
themes.body: The defense-tech IPO window is showing signs of life, suggesting that investors are cautiously optimistic about the sector's future. Meanwhile, the quiet review of Founders Fund's space portfolio hints at a strategic recalibration among venture capitalists.
